record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: For 0 < beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), a known radial result gives weak differentiability and the bound ||grad M_tilde_beta f||_{L^q(R^d)} <= C(d,beta)||grad f||_{L^1(R^d)} for radial f in W^{1,1}(R^d), where M_tilde_beta is the uncentered fractional maximal operator. Does the same statement hold for the centered fractional maximal operator M_beta acting on radial functions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 2$ and let $0<\beta<1$. For a locally integrable function $f\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ define the centered fractional Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator by
$$M_\beta f(x)\;=\;\sup_{r>0}\;\frac{1}{r^{d-\beta}}\int_{B(x,r)}|f(y)|\,dy,$$
where $B(x,r)$ is the open ball of radius $r$ centered at $x$ (so that for $\beta=0$ this reduces, up to a constant, to the usual centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function). Let $q=d/(d-\beta)$ and let $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the Sobolev space of integrable functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose distributional gradient lies in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$.

Question: Does there exist a constant $C=C(d,\beta)$ such that for every radial function $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the function $M_\beta f$ is weakly differentiable and
$$\|\nabla M_\beta f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)}\;\le\;C(d,\beta)\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The radial centered fractional endpoint bound was established by Beltrán and Madrid in "Regularity of the centered fractional maximal function on radial functions" (J. Funct. Anal., 2020), which proves the desired weak differentiability and gradient bound $\|\nabla M_\beta f\|_{L^q} \lesssim \|\nabla f\|_{L^1}$ for radial $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ in the range $0<\beta<1$. Subsequent work removed the radiality assumption in higher dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of the centered fractional maximal function on radial functions
status_evidence.snippet: The main new idea consists in relating the centered and non-centered fractional maximal function at the derivative level; the radiality assumption can be removed in certain cases.
status_evidence.claim: Answers the radial centered fractional endpoint question affirmatively for 0<beta<1.

status_evidence.title: Endpoint Sobolev Bounds for Fractional Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Operators (arXiv:2010.05561)
status_evidence.snippet: Both centered and uncentered fractional maximal operators satisfy the endpoint Sobolev bound; previously only known for radial functions when d>1 and alpha in (0,1).
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the radial centered case was already established and extends it to general functions.
